SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.claim: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة is cited as apposition to بالناصية, showing how a definite can be followed by an appositive description.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.claim: Taking someone by the forelock means seizing, raising, and humiliating its owner; the forelock stands for the person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r9.anchor: أي لنأخذن بها، ثم لنقيمنه ولنذلنه إما في الدنيا وإما في الآخرة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.claim: The oath-prefixed warning means that unless he stops, desists, repents, and submits before death, God will seize him by the forelock.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r8.anchor: اللام موطئة للقسم المضمر أي والله لئن لم ينته عما هو عليه ولم ينزجر ولم يتب ولم يسلم قبل الموت

BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.claim: The written alif in the emphatic verb represents the pause form of the light nūn; safʿ means seizing and pulling something harshly, and the forelock is the front hair.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r9.anchor: أصله لنسفعن بالنون الخفيفة للتأكيد ونظيره وليكونا من الصاغرين كتب في المصحف بالألف على حكم الوقف

BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.claim: The threat is to drag Abu Jahl by his forelock into Hell through the torment angels, humiliating him; Arabs treated seizure by the forelock as degrading subjugation.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r10.anchor: والمعنى لنأخذن في الآخرة بناصيته ولنسحبنه بها إلى النار بمعنى لتأمرن الزبانية ليأخذوا بناصيته ويجروه إلى النار

BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.claim: In ʿAyn al-Maʿānī, taking someone by the forelock is an expression of coercion and humiliation.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r11.anchor: وفي "عين المعاني" الأخذ بالناصية عبارة عن القهر والهوان

BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.claim: The forelock may also signify Abu Jahl being dragged face-first at Badr, when Muslims were enabled to seize him after he resumed forbidding prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من هذا السفع سحبه على وجهه في الدنيا يوم بدر فيكون بشارة بأن يمكن

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.claim: When no one else volunteered, Ibn Masʿūd offered to recite Sūrat al-Raḥmān to Quraysh; the Prophet initially feared for the small, weak Companion but eventually permitted him.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.anchor: روى) أنه لما نزلت سورة الرحمن ، قال عليه السلام : "من يقرأها على رؤساء قريش فتثاقلوا" فقام ابن

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd recited at the Kaaba; Abu Jahl slapped him, tearing and bloodying his ear, and he returned in tears while the Prophet grieved.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.anchor: فافتتح قراءة السورة فقام أبو جهل فلطمه فشق إذنه وادماها فانصرف وعينه تدمع فلما رآه عليه السلام رق قلبه

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.claim: Gabriel laughed at Ibn Masʿūd’s distress and said he would see what happened; at Badr, the Prophet sent Ibn Masʿūd to finish wounded survivors for a share in the reward of fighters.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.anchor: فإذا جبرائيل جاء ضاحكا مستبشرا فقال يا جبرائيل تضحك ويبكى ابن مسعود فقال سيعلم فلما ظفر المسلمون يوم بدر

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd found Abu Jahl alive and speared his neck from a distance, fearing he might still have strength; the author associates this with the later branding threat.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.anchor: فإذا أبو جهل مصروع يخور فخاف أن تكون به قوة فيؤذيه فوضع الرمح على منحره من بعيد فطعنه ولعل هذا قوله سنسمه على الخرطوم

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.claim: Too weak to climb Abu Jahl’s chest, Ibn Masʿūd used a ploy; Abu Jahl called him a shepherdling, and Ibn Masʿūd replied that Islam prevails and is not prevailed over.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.anchor: لم يقدر أن يصعد على صدره لضعفه فارتقى عليه بحيلة فلما رآه أبو جهل قال له يا رويعي الغنم لقد ارتقيت مرتقى

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.claim: Abu Jahl told Ibn Masʿūd to tell Muhammad that no one had been more hateful to him, even at death.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.anchor: فقال له أبو جهل بلغ صاحبك إنه لم يكن أحد أبغض إلى منه في حال مماتي

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.claim: The Prophet called Abu Jahl more defiant than Pharaoh, who at least professed belief, while Abu Jahl only increased in arrogance.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.anchor: فروى أنه عليه السلام لما سمع ذلك قال فرعوني أشد من فرعون موسى فإنه قال آمنت وهو قد زاد عتوا

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd cut off Abu Jahl’s head with his blunt sword, could not carry it, cut the ear, tied on a cord, and dragged it to the Prophet; Gabriel joked that it was ear for ear, though the head too was severed.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن مسعود اقطع بسيفي هذا لأنه أحد وأقطع فلما قطع رأسه لم يقدر

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says naṣiya can mean the forehead hair or the place where it grows, and here it stands for the face and head; Abu Jahl meticulously groomed his forelock.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ والناصية شعر الجبهة وقد يسمى مكان الشعر ناصية ثم إنه تعالى كنى بها ههنا عن الوجه والرأس ولعل السبب في تخصيص السفع

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r10.claim: The phrase “a lying, sinful forelock” is apposition to the earlier forelock; its indefinite adjective is permitted by description, and attributing lying and sin to the forelock intensifies the rhetoric.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r10.anchor: {ناصية كاذبة خاطئة} بدل من الناصية وإنما جاز أبدالها من المعرفة وهي نكرة لوصفها وصوف الناصية بالكذب والخطأ على الإسناد

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r11.claim: Abu Jahl lied about God not sending Muhammad and about Muhammad being a sorcerer, and sinned by harming him.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r11.anchor: وكان أبو جهل كاذبا على الله في أنه لم يرسل محمدا كاذبا في أنه ساحر ونحوه وخاطئا بما تعرض له عليه السلام بأنواع الأذية

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r16.claim: “A lying, sinful forelock” is grammatically an apposition to the forelock by which God threatens to seize him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r16.anchor: وقوله : { ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } بدل من قوله : { لنسفعا بالناصية

IBNASHUR:96:16/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:16/r1.claim: Nāṣiyah is an appositive to the forelock, made indefinite to refer to the class: a forelock of the lying, erring kind.
IBNASHUR:96:16/r1.anchor: بدل من الناصية وتنكيرها لاعتبار الجنس

IBNASHUR:96:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:16/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:16/r2.claim: Khāṭiʾah is the active participle of khaṭiʾa, to commit a sin; calling the forelock a liar and sinner is a rational metaphor for its owner.
IBNASHUR:96:16/r2.anchor: ووصفُ الناصية بالكاذبة والخاطئة مجاز عقلي . والمراد : كاذب صاحبُها خاطِىء صاحبها

IBNASHUR:96:16/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:16/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:16/r3.claim: The personification imagines the owner's lies and sins visibly emerging from his forehead, making the forelock fit for seizure.
IBNASHUR:96:16/r3.anchor: أنّ فيه تخييلاً بأن الكذب والخِطءَ بَاديان من ناصيته فكانت الناصية جديرة بالسفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.claim: The second “kalla” reinforces the first; placing one at the start created suspense, and the closing position is the natural place for its counterpart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r7.anchor: أكد الردع الأول بحرف الردع الثاني في آخر الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.claim: The warning follows as a threat if the offender does not desist; the lām introduces an oath, its answer is “we will seize,” and the conditional answer is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r8.anchor: وأما جواب الشرط فمحذوف دل عليه جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.claim: Seizing means gripping and pulling forcefully; taking someone by the forelock signifies dragging him to punishment and humiliating him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r9.anchor: والأخذ من الناصية أخذ من لا يترك له تمكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.claim: The added bāʾ strengthens the sense of contact in the seizure; the light emphatic nūn commonly follows positive oaths and is written as an alif to reflect pausal pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r10.anchor: وأكد ذلك السفع بالباء المزيدة الداخلة على المفعول لتأكيد اللصوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.claim: The light emphatic nūn often enters affirmative oaths and is written as an alif in the muṣḥaf to reflect its pronunciation at pause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r11.anchor: والنون نون التوكيد الخفيفة التي يكثر دخولها في القسم المثبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.claim: The definite forelock is anaphoric, meaning the forelock of the man who forbids prayer; Kufan grammarians call the lām a substitute for the genitive pronoun, while Basrans posit an attachment for the lām’s complement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r1.anchor: والتعريف في ( الناصية ) للعهد التقديري ، أي بناصيته ، أي ناصية الذي ينهى عبدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.claim: “A forelock, lying, sinful” is an indefinite appositive referring to the generic kind; describing it as lying and sinful is a rhetorical attribution to its owner, imagining his sins visible on his forelock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r2.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكاذبة والخاطئة مجاز عقلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيوة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r11.claim: Abu Haywa reads the three adjectives in the accusative, while a report says al-Kisai reads them all nominative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: «ناصية كاذبة خاطئة» بالنصب في الثلاثة، وروي عن الكسائي أنه قرأ بالرفع فيها كلها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r12.claim: The forelock is the front of the head's hair; an indefinite noun restates the definite one, while lying and error describe its owner, like calling a hand thieving.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r12.anchor: والناصية مقدم شعر الرأس، ثم أبدل النكرة من المعرفة في قوله: ناصية كاذبة ووصفها بالكذب والخطإ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says ناصية is a genitive substitute for the preceding word.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة هي بدل فلذلك جرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the forelock's owner is the liar and sinner, as in saying that a day fasts when one means its owner fasts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج والمعنى بناصية صاحبها كاذب خاطىء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r7.claim: The lying, erring forelock means Abu Jahl lies in speech and errs in action.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r7.anchor: يعني: ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في مقالها خاطئة في فعالها.

FARRA:v3p279/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p279/r1.claim: Repeating nāṣiya is emphasis: a definite expression can repeat a prior indefinite one, as “a straight path, the path of God.”
FARRA:v3p279/r1.anchor: على التكرير، كما قال: «إلى صراط مستقيم، صراط الله » المعرفة ترد على النكرة بالتكرير،

FARRA:v3p279/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p279/r2.claim: Accusative nāṣiyatan is also a valid reading, treating it as the object of an implied verb.
FARRA:v3p279/r2.anchor: على المعرفة، ومن نصب (ناصية) جعله فعلا للمعرفة وهي جائزة في القراءة

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r1.claim: The second nāṣiya is appositional to the first; its description as lying and sinful really describes its owner, by extension as in “fasting day.”
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r1.anchor: ثم وصف ناصية ذلك الكافر فقال: ناصية وهي بدل من الناصية الأولى كأنه خاطبها

KASHSHAF:96:16/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:16/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:16/r1.claim: Nasiyaa is apposition to the definite forelock; a descriptive indefinite phrase can have enough independent meaning to serve as its appositive.
KASHSHAF:96:16/r1.anchor: بدل من الناصية ؛ وجاز بدلها عن المعرفة

KASHSHAF:96:16/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:16/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:16/r2.claim: Nominative or accusative readings also work as an insult, either as an implied sentence or direct insult.

KASHSHAF:96:16/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:16/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:16/r3.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful is a figurative attribution to its owner and is more vivid than directly describing him.
KASHSHAF:96:16/r3.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطإ على الإسناد المجازي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r4.claim: Nasiyatun apposes the definite forelock despite being indefinite because its description informs; nominative or accusative readings work as an insult.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r4.anchor: { ناصية } بدل من الناصية ؛ جاز بدلها عن المعرفة ، وهي نكرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r5.claim: Calling the forelock lying and mistaken is a figurative attribution; its owner is actually the liar and wrongdoer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r5.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطأ على الإسناد المجازي

MAJAZ:v2p304/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p304/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p304/r4.claim: Nāṣiyatin kādhibatin is an appositional substitute (badal) for fajrahā.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r1.claim: The naṣiya is the hair at the front of the head, and can figuratively mean the whole person, as in calling a person a blessed forelock.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r1.anchor: والناصية شعر مقدم الرأس , وقد يعبر بها عن جملة الإنسان , كما يقال هذه ناصية مباركة إشارة إلى جميع الإنسان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r2.claim: The forelock of Abu Jahl is called lying in its speech and erring in its action.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r2.anchor: ثم قال : { ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } يعني ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في قولها , خاطئة في فعلها .

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r9.claim: The threat of return to God warns Abū Jahl about the Resurrection; the forelock threat later names him, and the following verse calls that forelock lying and sinful.

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.claim: If Abū Jahl does not stop his denial and turning away from Muhammad, God will seize his forelock forcefully; angels drag him face-first into the Fire for his sin, since the forelock is described as lying and sinful.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r4.anchor: لنأخذن بالناصية أخذا شديدا، ثم أخبر عنه أنه فاجر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#10/r1.claim: “A lying, sinful forelock” apposes the earlier forelock and attributes its owner's lying and sin to it figuratively, a more forceful expression than describing the person directly.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#10/r1.anchor: ﴿ ناصية ﴾ بدل من الناصية لأنها وصفت بالكذب والخطأ بقوله ﴿ كاذبة خاطئة ﴾

NAHHAS:v5p261/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r19.claim: Al-nāṣiyah is an appositive substitute; al-Farrāʾ calls it repetition, and an indefinite nāṣiyah kādhibah khāṭiʾah may follow a definite noun.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r19.anchor: على البدل والفراء يقول على التكرير وأجاز ( ناصية كاذبة خاطئة ) لأنها نكرة بعد معرفة

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.claim: Although the threat concerns Abu Jahl, it warns everyone who refuses obedience or prevents others from obeying.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r2.anchor: فالآية وإن كانت في أبي جهل فهي عظة للناس، وتهديد لمن يمتنع أو يمنع غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r8.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful means its owner lies in speech and sins in action; a khati' is culpable, unlike a nonculpable mukhti'.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r8.anchor: أي ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في قولها، خاطئة في فعلها. والخاطىء معاقب

QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r9.claim: The attribution of lying and sin to the forelock is like describing faces as gazing toward their Lord, or saying a day fasts and a night stands for the person who fasts and prays.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:15-16/r9.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكاذبة الخاطئة، كوصف الوجوه بالنظر في قوله تعالى:

QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:15/r2.claim: Safʿ means seizing violently; the forehead is the arrogant tyrant's raised, forward, conspicuous part.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:16/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:16/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:16/r1.claim: This lying, sinful forehead deserves to be seized and cast down; the wording evokes the moment of violent seizure and overthrow.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:16/r1.anchor: إنها ناصية تستحق السفع والصرع :  ( ناصية كاذبة خاطئة )

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.claim: The definite forelock is physically known but its attributes are newly exposed: it is false in speech and sinful in action.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r2.anchor: الناصية المعروفة عندكم ذاتها لكنها مجهولة عندكم صفاتها

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r3.claim: The forelock is called lying because Abu Jahl lied about God not sending Muhammad and called the Messenger a sorcerer, liar, or non-prophet; another explanation is his boast of having the largest assembly.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r3.anchor: وإنما وصف بالكذب لأنه كان كاذبا على الله تعالى في أنه لم يرسل محمدا

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r4.claim: It is called sinful because its owner rebels against God; khāṭiʾ is culpable, unlike mukhṭiʾ, who is not held to account, and the adjective follows the usage of describing faces as gazing.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r4.anchor: والفرق بين الخاطىء والمخطىء أن الخاطىء معاقب مؤاخذ

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r5.claim: The second naṣiya is an appositive for the definite first one; an indefinite can replace a definite when it is qualified and supplies an independent point.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r5.anchor: { ناصية } بدل من الناصية ، وجاز إبدالها من المعرفة وهي نكرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r6.claim: The reading with nominative naṣiya implies ‘it is a forelock’; the accusative and nominative can both serve as invective.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r6.anchor: قرىء ناصية بالرفع والتقدير هي ناصية ، وناصية بالنصب

SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī justifies the indefinite adjective phrase nāṣiyatin kādhibatin as apposition to a definite noun because its description makes it informative; the author notes this is the Kufan rule, unlike the Basran one.
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r1.anchor: وجاز بدلها عن المعرفة وهي نكرة لأنها وصفت فاستقلت بفائدة

SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r2.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read nāṣiyatan kādhibatan khāṭiʾatan in the accusative as an insult; al-Kisāʾī has a nominative with omitted hiya.
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي بنصب " ناصية كاذبة خاطئة " على الشتم

SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r3.claim: Calling the forelock deceitful and sinful is figurative; the definite article may replace annexation or conceal an omitted pronoun meaning his forelock.
SAMIN-DURR:96:16/r3.anchor: ونسب الكذب والخطأ إليها مجازا. والألف واللام في الناصية قيل: عوض من الإضافة

TAB-FULL:v24p537/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r1.claim: The second forelock is genitive by repetition of the first, while lying and sinful describe its owner.
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r1.anchor: فليدع أبو جهل أهل مجلسه وأنصاره، من عشيرته وقومه، والنادي: هو المجلس

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p541/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p541/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p541/r1.claim: “No” denies Abu Jahl’s claim as he forbids Muhammad from worship and prayer.
TAB-FULL:v24p541/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: ليس الأمر كما يقول أبو جهل، إذ ينهى محمدا عن عبادة ربه، والصلاة له

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r5.claim: Calling the forehead deceitful and sinful is figurative: those qualities belong to its owner.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r5.anchor: وفي توصيف الناصية بالكذب والخطأ وهما وصفا صاحب الناصية مجاز

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r5.claim: The lying, sinful forelock means its owner is a liar and sinner, like saying someone's day fasts and night prays.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r5.anchor:
وتأويله بناصية صاحبها كاذب خاطئ، كما يقال فلان نهاره صائم وليله
قائم، المعنى هو صائم في نهاره وقائم في ليله.

TABRISI:96:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r4.claim: The forehead lock is hair at the front of the head, so named for being attached to it; the root denotes joining.
TABRISI:96:2/r4.anchor: والناصية شعر مقدم الرأس سميت بذلك لأنها متصلة بالرأس

TABRISI:96:2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r5.speaker: الراجز
TABRISI:96:2/r5.claim: An anonymous rajaz poet uses tanasiha in a line as evidence for the root meaning of joining.
TABRISI:96:2/r5.anchor: سميت بذلك لأنها متصلة بالرأس من قولهم ناصى يناصي مناصاة إذا وصل قال الراجز

TABRISI:96:2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r13.claim: Nasiyah is an apposition explaining the forehead lock as its owner's lying, erring head, like saying a person's day fasts and night stands in prayer.
TABRISI:96:2/r13.anchor: بناصية صاحبها كاذب خاطىء يقال فلان نهاره صائم

TABRISI:96:16-19/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:96:16-19/r2.claim: When Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet and boasted that no one had a larger council, the Prophet rebuked him; the passage about calling his gathering was revealed.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r2.anchor: لما أتى أبو جهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهره رسول الله

TABRISI:96:16-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:16-19/r3.claim: The forehead lock is described as lying and erring to mean that its owner lies in speech and errs in actions.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r3.anchor: وصفها بالكذب والخطأ بمعنى أن صاحبها كاذب في أقواله خاطىء في أفعاله

THALABI:v10p246/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p246/r5.claim: The threat to seize the forelock means taking the front of his head and humiliating him; “lying, sinful forelock” renames the person by his trait.
THALABI:v10p246/r5.anchor: لنسفعا بالناصية لنأخذن بمقدم رأسه فلنذلنه، ثم قال على البدل: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r1.claim: The forelock is described as lying about God and being polytheistic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: كاذبة على الله مشركة (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r2.claim: The second “forelock” is an apposition to the first; the description of the forelock means its owner is a liar and wrongdoer, as in calling a person “his day fasting.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ناصية بدل من الناصية، المعنى: لنسفعا بناصية (¬6) كاذبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r3.claim: After Muḥammad rebuked Abū Jahl for forbidding prayer, Abū Jahl boasted that no one had a larger council than he; Ibn ʿAbbās says the threat passage was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نهى أبو جهل رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- (عن) (¬8) الصلاة انتهره رسول الله

WAHIDI-QT:96:16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:16/r1.claim: The forelock is called lying and sinful, meaning its owner is a liar and offender.
WAHIDI-QT:96:16/r1.anchor: ثم وصف ناصيته فقال { ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } وتأويلها صاحبها كاذب خاطىء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r8.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful describes its owner as a liar and sinner.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r8.anchor: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } وتأويلها: صاحبها كاذب خاطىء.

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.claim: Nasiyah means the hair or forelock on the forehead and can also name the forehead or front of the head; here it is a metonym for the head and therefore the person.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r1.anchor: “Nâsıye” mâlum ki alındaki saç, perçem demektir. Onun bittiği cebheye, alına, yani alnın üstünde başın ön tarafına dahi ıtlak olunur. Burada murad baştan ve dolayısıyla şahıstan kinayedir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r2.claim: The indefinite apposition generalizes the threat; “lying, sinful” both justifies the dragging and clarifies that the person, who actually lies and sins, is meant, though the literal forelock remains possible too.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r2.anchor: Yalancı, hatîekâr; cânî bir nâsıyeyi bu bedelin nekre olarak getirilmesi emsâline ta‘mîm içindir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.claim: Seizing the forelock is figurative; explanations include taking the offender to Hell, disgracing him, stamping his forehead, or humiliating him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r1.anchor: “Onu tutup cehenneme atacağız, yüzünü kara çıkaracağız, alnını damgalayacağız, alçaltacağız” gibi değişik şekillerde açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.claim: A self-satisfied tyrant who blocks worship may be left free for a time, but will ultimately be caught and punished in this world, the Hereafter, or both; Abu Jahl and others suffered defeat here and will face the promised afterlife punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:15/r2.anchor: sonunda bir gün gelip yakasına yapışılacağı, hak ettiği cezayı göreceği bildirilmektedir

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-16:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-16:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Ibn Masʿūd
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-16:anmerkung/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd transmits fāǧira as a variant in place of ḫāṭiʾa.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-16:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Von Ibn Masʿūd wird die Variante fāǧira statt ḫāṭiʾa überliefert

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r4.claim: The second ‘forelock’ is grammatically a بدل of the preceding definite forelock; it can count as definite through its adjective despite lacking the article.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r4.anchor: Though the former is not defined by the article alif

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.claim: The harsh wording conveys anger; the forehead represents a person’s honor, and the prostration mark is its greatest honor, so one who refuses prostration and prevents others deserves Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r5.anchor: the greatest honour for a forehead is the mark of prostration that becomes stamped on it

QIRAAT-ER:96:16:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:16:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:16:3#1/r1.claim: The ten-reader variant drops hamza and substitutes yāʾ, a recognized dialectal hamza treatment that is semantically identical.
QIRAAT-ER:96:16:3#1/r1.anchor: hamza dropped, yāʾ substituted — khāṭiyatin instead of khāṭiʾatin

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r9.claim: The majority read nāṣiyatin, kādhibatin, khāṭiʾatin in the genitive, parsing the indefinite nāṣiya as an appositive to the definite one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ناصية، كاذبة خاطئة، بجر الثلاثة على أن ناصية بدل نكرة من معرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the adjective allows the indefinite appositive to stand independently with useful meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: لأنها وصفت فاستقلت بفائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r11.claim: The author says Basran grammarians do not require such an appositive to be described, nor that it repeat the wording of its antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r11.anchor: وليس شرطا في إبدال النكرة من المعرفة أن توصف عند البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r12.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r12.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read the three words in the accusative as invective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي: بنصب الثلاثة على الشتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r13.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r13.claim: Al-Kisāʾī in one transmission reads the words in the nominative, with an understood predicate: “it is a forelock.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r13.anchor: والكسائي في رواية: برفعها، أي هي ناصبة كاذبة خاطئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r14.claim: Calling the forelock lying and erring is figurative because its owner lies and errs; the construction is preferable because the forelock is the topic already introduced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r14.anchor: وصفها بالكذب والخطأ مجازا، والحقيقة صاحبها، وذلك أحرى من أن يضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r1.claim: Nāṣiyatin is an appositive to the definite nāṣiya; its modifiers make the indefinite informative. Basrans require informativeness, while Kufans require matching form and a descriptive modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r1.anchor: ناصية بدل من الناصية وجاز إبدالها عن المعرفة وهي نكرة لأنها وصفت بقوله سبحانه كاذبة خاطئة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r2.claim: Calling the forelock itself lying and erring intensifies the owner's traits, as though every part lies and sins; this is figurative attribution of the whole's quality to a part, as in 16:62.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r2.anchor: ووصف الناصية بما ذكر مع أنه صفة صاحبها للمبالغة حيث يدل على وصفه بالكذب والخطأ بطريق الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن عبلة وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn ʿAbla, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī put all three words in the accusative as an insult; al-Kisāʾī has a nominative reading, understood as She is a lying, sinful forelock.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن عبلة وزيد بن علي ناصية كاذبة خاطئة ينصب الثلاثة على الشتم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r9.claim: The forelock is called lying and sinful by substitution, meaning its owner is a liar and sinner.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r9.anchor: ثم قال على البدل: {ناصية كاذبة خاطئة} أي صاحبها كاذب خاطئ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad with a large clan, cavalry, and armed men after Muhammad rebuked him for stopping prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نهى أبو جهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة انتهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r2.claim: The lying, sinning forelock renames the forelock in apposition; its traits are figuratively attributed from its owner for emphasis, and it may be read in nominative or accusative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r2.anchor: بدل من الناصية وإنما جاز لوصفها، وقرئت بالرفع على هي ناصية

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head and can stand for the face, anything foremost, or the leading people of a community.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r4.anchor: والناصية قصاصة الشعر في مقدمة الرأس. ويستغنى بالناصية مجازاً عن الوجه

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r7.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful invokes the Quran’s predominant religious sense of disbelief and misguidance.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r7.anchor: بدلالتها الإسلامية الخاصة على الكفر والضلال، وهي الدلالة الغالبة في الاستعمال القرآني

BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r6.claim: The forelock is described as deliberately lying and committing other sins without intent as well; this mixture reflects its owner's corrupt disposition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r6.anchor: فهي صادر عنها الذنب من الكذب وغيره من غير تعمد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r7.claim: Calling the forelock itself a liar and sinner is figurative attribution to its owner and heightens the eloquence and severity of the threat.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p486/r7.anchor: ووصفها بما هو لصاحبها على الإسناد المجازي مبالغة في تكذيبه

SIBAWAYH:شبهوهبمايشبهمنالأسماءبالمصادرنح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:شبهوهبمايشبهمنالأسماءبالمصادرنح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:شبهوهبمايشبهمنالأسماءبالمصادرنح.claim: The Qur'anic al-nāṣiyati nāṣiyatin kādhibatin supplies an example of an accusative noun followed by an appositional clarification.
SIBAWAYH:شبهوهبمايشبهمنالأسماءبالمصادرنح.anchor: كما قال عز وجل @QB@ بالناصية ناصية كاذبة @QE@

TAB:96:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:16/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:16/r1.claim: The genitive ‘forelock’ repeats and apposes the earlier ‘forelock’ in the preceding verse.
TAB:96:16/r1.anchor: فخفض ناصية ردا على الناصية الأولى بالتكرير

TAB:96:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:16/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:16/r2.claim: The forelock is called lying and sinful, while the intended referent is its owner.
TAB:96:16/r2.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكذب والخطيئة ،   والمعنى لصاحبها

BURHAN:v2p455/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.claim: Part and inclusion substitutes clarify and specify an antecedent by naming it twice, first generally and then particularly; the forelock example adds its quality as the reason for seizing it.
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.anchor: وفائدة البدل أن ذلك الشيء يصير مذكورا مرتين إحداهما بالعموم والثانية بالخصوص

BURHAN:v2p455/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r6.speaker: ابن يعيش
BURHAN:v2p455/r6.claim: Ibn Yaʿish says an indefinite substitute for a definite is not good unless qualified, as in the described forelock, because the clarification depends on both.
BURHAN:v2p455/r6.anchor: قال ابن يعيش ولا يحسن بدل النكرة من المعرفة حتى توصف كالآية لأن البيان مرتبط بهما جميعا

BURHAN:v2p268/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p268/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p268/r3.claim: A part may receive the whole’s quality: error describes the whole person, while falsehood is specifically the tongue’s quality, yet both qualify the forehead metonymically.
BURHAN:v2p268/r3.anchor: الخطأ صفة الكل فوصف به الناصية وأما الكاذبة فصفة اللسان

ITQAN:v3p99/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r1.claim: The whole person's quality of error is attributed to his forelock, describing a part with the quality of the whole.
ITQAN:v3p99/r1.anchor: فالخطأ صفة الكل وصف به الناصية عكسه كقوله ﴿ إنا منكم وجلون ﴾

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمجرىنعتالمعرفةعليها)#206.claim: He uses 96:15–16 to illustrate the second definite “ناصية” as appositional to “الناصية,” with “كاذبة خاطئة” describing it.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p931/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p931/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p931/r3.claim: Badal may serve praise or blame; ناصية كاذبة خاطئة is blame, while وهذا البلد الأمين exemplifies praise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p931/r3.anchor: قد يكون للمدح أو الذمّ كما في قوله تعالى

NASHR:v1p395#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p395#2/r1.claim: With a fatḥah hamza preceded by ḍammah at a verb's start, Abū Jaʿfar and Warsh generally replace it with wāw.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r1.anchor: فاتفق أبو جعفر وورش على إبدالها واوا نحو

NASHR:v1p395#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r2.speaker: ابن وردان
NASHR:v1p395#2/r2.claim: Ibn Wardān differs on yuʾayyid bi-naṣrihi: some routes preserve hamza, apparently to avoid three weak letters in succession after the doubled yāʾ, while most substitute wāw in line with the rule.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r2.anchor: واختلف ابن وردان في حرف واحد من ذلك، وهو (يؤيد بنصره) في آل عمران، فروى ابن شبيب

NASHR:v1p395#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r3.speaker: ورش
NASHR:v1p395#2/r3.claim: For muʾadhdhin, al-Aṣbahānī preserves Warsh's hamza, apparently because of its link with fa-adhdhin; al-Azraq instead substitutes according to the usual rule.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r3.anchor: واختلف أيضا عن ورش في حرف واحد، وهو (مؤذن) في الأعراف ويوسف. فروى عنه الأصبهاني

NASHR:v1p395#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r4.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v1p395#2/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ uniquely replaces a final root hamza in huzuwan at ten occurrences and also in kufuwan.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r4.anchor: فإن حفصا اختص بإبدالها في (هزوا) ، وهو في عشرة مواضع

NASHR:v1p395#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v1p395#2/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar commonly changes an open hamza preceded by kasrah to yāʾ, including khāṭiʾah; some routes of Ibn Wardān and Zayd preserve hamza in khāṭiʾah, al-khāṭiʾah, miʾah, and fiʾah.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك (يبدلها) في (خاطئة، والخاطئة، ومئة، وفئة) وتثنيتهما، وانفرد الشطوي عن ابن هارون

NASHR:v1p395#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p395#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p395#2/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar's reading of mawṭiyan varies among transmitters: some report substitution and some hamza; the author accepts both, has read both, and adopts both.
NASHR:v1p395#2/r6.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان، بهما قرأت، وبهما آخذ، والله أعلم.

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r1.claim: The majority read all three words in the genitive, treating nāṣiya as an indefinite appositive to the definite forelock.
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r1.anchor: { ناصية . . . خاطئة } ، بجر الثلاثة على أن ناصية بدل نكرة من معرفة

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the indefinite appositive is acceptable because it is qualified and thus contributes new information.
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري : لأنها وصفت فاستقبلت بفائدة

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that Basran grammarians do not require an indefinite appositive to be qualified; it also need not repeat the wording of its antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r3.anchor: وليس شرطاً في إبدال النكرة من المعرفة أن توصف عند البصريين خلافاً لمن شرط ذلك من غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r4.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read all three words in the accusative as an insult.
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي : بنصب الثلاثة على الشتم

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r5.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r5.claim: In one transmission, al-Kisāʾī reads the words in the nominative, construing the phrase as “it is a lying, sinful forelock.”
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r5.anchor: والكسائي في رواية : برفعها ، أي هي ناصبة كاذبة خاطئة

ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r6.claim: Calling the forelock a liar and sinner is figurative, since its owner is the actual liar and sinner; this is more fitting because the forelock is the subject already named in verse 15.
ABUHAYYAN:96:16/r6.anchor: وصفها بالكذب والخطأ مجازاً ، والحقيقة صاحبها ، وذلك أحرى من أن يضاف

ALUSI:96:16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:16/r1.claim: Nāṣiyatin is an appositive to the definite al-nāṣiya; the adjective makes the indefinite informative. Basrans require only informative value for indefinite apposition, while Kufans also require matching wording and an adjective.
ALUSI:96:16/r1.anchor: بدل من { الناصية } وجاز إبدالها عن المعرفة وهي نكرة

ALUSI:96:16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:16/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:16/r2.claim: Calling the forelock a liar and sinner intensifies the owner's traits, as if each part lied and sinned; this is figurative attribution of a whole's quality to a part, like 16:62 and the idiom that a face describes beauty.
ALUSI:96:16/r2.anchor: ووصف الناصية بما ذكر مع أنه صفة صاحبها للمبالغة حيث يدل على وصفه بالكذب والخطأ

ALUSI:96:16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:16/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة
ALUSI:96:16/r3.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd b. ʿAlī read all three words in the accusative as an insult; al-Kisāʾī has a report with all three raised, understood as hiya nāṣiyatun.
ALUSI:96:16/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي ناصية كاذبة خاطئة بنصب الثلاثة على الشتم

BAGHAWI:96:16/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:16/r1.claim: The phrase “a lying, sinful forelock” is in apposition; the description means that its owner is a liar and sinner.
BAGHAWI:96:16/r1.anchor: ثم قال على البدل :{ ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } أي صاحبها كاذب خاطئ

BAGHAWI:96:16/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:16/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:96:16/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Prophet rebuked Abu Jahl for forbidding prayer, Abu Jahl threatened to fill the valley with swift horses and strong men.
BAGHAWI:96:16/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : " لما نهى أبو جهل الرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة انتهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI:96:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:16/r1.claim: The phrase is an apposition to the preceding forelock; the apposition is permitted because it is qualified.
BAYDAWI:96:16/r1.anchor: { ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } بدل من الناصية ، وإنما جاز لوصفها

BAYDAWI:96:16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:16/r2.speaker: قرئ
BAYDAWI:96:16/r2.claim: It is also read in the nominative, understood as ‘it is a forelock,’ or in the accusative as a form of blame.
BAYDAWI:96:16/r2.anchor: وقرئت بالرفع على هي ناصية ، والنصب على الذم

BAYDAWI:96:16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:16/r3.claim: Calling the forelock lying and erring ascribes its owner’s qualities to it metaphorically for emphasis.
BAYDAWI:96:16/r3.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطأ وهما لصاحبها على الإسناد المجازي للمبالغة

BIQAI:96:16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:16/r1.claim: The forelock phrase is a substitute, its form bringing it closer to definiteness; capture in this humiliating posture already implies death, so the verse need not add that he will be dragged face-first to Hell.
BIQAI:96:16/r1.anchor: ولما كان من المعلوم أن من صار في القبضة على هذه الهيئة المهينة المزرية فهو هالك

BIQAI:96:16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:16/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:16/r2.claim: The forelock is called lying because its owner lies deliberately; it is called erring because he sins without intending to, with most of his conduct unsound either way due to his bad nature.
BIQAI:96:16/r2.anchor: فهي صادرة عنها الذنب من الكذب وغيره

BIQAI:96:16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:16/r3.claim: Attributing the owner's lying and sin to the forelock is figurative emphasis; it denies his power to harm the guided person except by God's permission, which may make the harm a cause of the victim's elevation.
BIQAI:96:16/r3.anchor: ووصفها بما هو لصاحبها على الإسناد المجازي مبالغة في تكذيبه في أنه لا يقدر على منع المهتدي

BIQAI:96:16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:16/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:16/r4.claim: Calling the forelock itself a liar and sinner is more forceful and eloquent than directly describing its owner as a lying sinner.
BIQAI:96:16/r4.anchor: من الجزالة والفخامة والجلالة ما لا يخفى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.claim: Sībawayh cites ‘by the forelock, a lying forelock’ to show that the second nominative can be apposition (badal) to the first, one of four analyses of the raised construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.anchor: هذا زيد رجل منطلق على البدل

IBNATIYYA:96:15/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r8.claim: Ibn Masud’s codex reads la-asfaʿanna bi-l-nāṣiya, nāṣiya kādhiba fājira.
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r8.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود : «لأسفعن بالناصية ناصية كاذبة فاجرة »

IBNATIYYA:96:15/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r9.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r9.claim: Abu Haywa reads nāṣiyatan kādhibatan khāṭiʾatan with all three words in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة : «ناصيةً كاذبةً خاطئةً » بالنصب في الثلاثة

IBNATIYYA:96:15/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r10.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r10.claim: Al-Kisaʾi is reported to read all three words in the nominative.
IBNATIYYA:96:15/r10.anchor: وروي عن الكسائي أنه قرأ بالرفع فيها كلها

IBNATIYYA:96:16/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r1.claim: Nāṣiya is an indefinite noun substituted for the preceding definite noun.
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r1.anchor: ثم أبدل النكرة من المعرفة في قوله : { ناصية كاذبة }

IBNATIYYA:96:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r2.claim: The forelock is called lying and erring by attributing its owner's traits to it, like calling a hand thieving.
IBNATIYYA:96:16/r2.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطإ من حيث صفة لصاحبها ، كما تقول : يد سارقة

IBNKATHIR:96:16/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:16/r1.claim: The forelock belongs to Abu Jahl: it is false in its speech and sinful in its deeds.
IBNKATHIR:96:16/r1.anchor: ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في مقالها خاطئة في فعَالها

MAWARDI:96:16/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:16/r1.claim: The forelock is Abu Jahl's: it is called lying for his speech and errant for his actions.
MAWARDI:96:16/r1.anchor: قال : { ناصيةٍ كاذبةٍ خاطئةٍ } يعني ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في قولها ، خاطئة في فعلها .

NASAFI:96:16/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:16/r1.claim: “A lying, sinful forelock” is an apposition to the forelock mentioned before.
NASAFI:96:16/r1.anchor: { نَاصِيَةٍ } بدل من { الناصية } لأنها وصفت بالكذب والخطأ

NASAFI:96:16/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:16/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:16/r2.claim: The adjectives transfer lying and sin figuratively from the owner to his forelock; this is more elegant and forceful than calling him a liar and sinner directly.
NASAFI:96:16/r2.anchor: عن الإسناد المجازي وهما لصاحبها حقيقة

QURTUBI:96:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:16/r1.claim: The phrase describes Abu Jahl’s forehead: its owner lies in speech and sins in action.
QURTUBI:96:16/r1.anchor: أي ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في قولها

QURTUBI:96:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:16/r2.claim: A deliberate wrongdoer is punishable, unlike someone who means right but makes a mistake.
QURTUBI:96:16/r2.anchor: والخاطئ معاقب مأخوذ .   والمخطئ غير مأخوذ

QURTUBI:96:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:16/r3.claim: Attributing lying and sin to the forehead parallels describing faces as looking in 75:23.
QURTUBI:96:16/r3.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكاذبة الخاطئة ،   كوصف الوجوه بالنظر

QURTUBI:96:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:16/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:16/r4.claim: The wording can describe the owner as liar and sinner, like saying his day fasts and his night stands in prayer.
QURTUBI:96:16/r4.anchor: أي صاحبها كاذب خاطئ ،   كما يقال : نهاره صائم

RAZI:96:15/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r24.claim: The definite forelock is familiar in identity but unknown in its qualities: what a forelock, false in speech and sinful in deed.
RAZI:96:15/r24.anchor: المسألة الخامسة : أنه تعالى عرف الناصية بحرف التعريف كأنه تعالى يقول : الناصية المعروفة عندكم ذاتها لكنها مجهولة عندكم صفاتها ناصية وأي ناصية

RAZI:96:15/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r25.claim: The forelock is called lying because its owner falsely denied that God sent Muhammad and called the Prophet a sorcerer, liar, or no prophet.
RAZI:96:15/r25.anchor: وإنما وصف بالكذب لأنه كان كاذبا على الله تعالى في أنه لم يرسل محمدا وكاذبا على رسوله

RAZI:96:15/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r26.claim: Another explanation links the lie to Abu Jahl's boast that he had the largest assembly in the valley.
RAZI:96:15/r26.anchor: وقيل : كذبه أنه قال : أنا أكثر أهل هذا الوادي ناديا

RAZI:96:15/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r27.claim: The forelock is sinful because its owner rebelled against God; Razi cites the verse saying only wrongdoers eat it.
RAZI:96:15/r27.anchor: ووصف الناصية بأنها خاطئة لأن صاحبها متمرد على الله تعالى قال الله تعالى : { لا يأكله إلا الخاطئون }

RAZI:96:15/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r28.claim: A khāṭiʾ is culpable and punished, unlike a mukhṭiʾ, whose mistake is not held against him.
RAZI:96:15/r28.anchor: والفرق بين الخاطئ والمخطئ أن الخاطئ معاقب مؤاخذ والمخطئ غير مؤاخذ

RAZI:96:15/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:15/r29.speaker: author
RAZI:96:15/r29.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful attributes the owner's qualities to his body part, just as faces are described as gazing in 75:23.
RAZI:96:15/r29.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالخاطئة الكاذبة كما وصف الوجوه بأنها ناظرة في قوله تعالى : { إلى ربها ناظرة }

RAZI:96:16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r1.claim: Nāṣiyatin substitutes for the definite al-nāṣiya; an indefinite can replace a definite here because its description makes it independently informative.
RAZI:96:16/r1.anchor: المسألة السادسة : { ناصية } بدل من الناصية ، وجاز إبدالها من المعرفة وهي نكرة ، لأنها وصفت فاستقلت بفائدة

RAZI:96:16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r2.claim: Nāṣiya is read in the nominative, understood as “it is a forelock,” or in the accusative; both forms are used as an insult.
RAZI:96:16/r2.anchor: المسألة السابعة : قرئ ناصية بالرفع والتقدير هي ناصية ، وناصية بالنصب وكلاهما على الشتم
